claims.text: CrMnFeCoNi or FeCoCrNiMn can serve as a high-entropy-alloy bond coat in a thermal barrier coating system.
Approximately 4 wt% ZrC can be incorporated by co-sputtering or precursor-powder addition during plasma transferred arc spraying.
The proposed processing routes will form finely dispersed ZrC particles in situ within the HEA bond coat.
A low volume fraction of in situ ZrC will improve the high-temperature durability and reliability of the HEA bond coat.
Dispersed ZrC will retard oxidation of the HEA bond coat under thermal cycling.
Dispersed ZrC will minimize phase degradation of the HEA bond coat under thermal cycling.
Temperatures from 500 °C to 900 °C are representative of high-temperature TBC operation.
ZrC particulates act as a diffusion barrier that impedes oxygen ingress.
ZrC particles pin grain boundaries in the HEA matrix.
Grain-boundary pinning by ZrC reduces grain growth and phase changes during thermal cycling.
The ZrC-modified coating will develop a thinner, more protective oxide scale than the untreated coating.
The ZrC-modified bond coat will have better adhesion to the ceramic top coat than the untreated bond coat.
The ZrC-modified coating will retain higher microhardness during prolonged high-temperature exposure and thermal cycling.
Durability improvement requires an optimized, relatively low ZrC content.
Excessive ZrC or poor ZrC dispersion could cause embrittlement or a non-uniform phase distribution.
The durability benefit may not persist under thermal shock more extreme than ordinary TBC operating conditions.
Prior evidence shows that ZrC addition improves the aqueous corrosion resistance of CrMnFeCoNi/FeCoCrNiMn HEA coatings in aggressive NaCl environments.
